extracted.intended_audience: HUD program officials, regional administrators, grant recipients and Certifying Officers responsible for environmental review and compliance with floodplain and wetland protections (24 CFR part 55/part 58)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for HUD and HUD-assisted grant recipients to determine applicability, perform environmental review, make decisions, document actions, and impose restrictions when proposed HUD financial assistance or activities are located in floodplains, coastal high hazard areas, floodways, or wetlands (implementation of Executive Orders 11988 & 11990).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability determination (whether EO 11988/11990 and this part apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before reaching decision points, HUD or the grant recipient shall determine whether Executive Orders 11988 and 11990 and 24 CFR part 55 apply to the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either Executive Order applies, approval or initial commitment must follow this part. The primary purpose of EO 11988 is to avoid direct or indirect support of floodplain development; under EO 11990 the decision process applies to Federal assistance for new construction in wetland locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition under Flood Disaster Protection Act for non‑NFIP communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed HUD financial assistance for acquisition or construction in any FEMA-designated area having special flood hazards shall not be approved in communities identified by FEMA as eligible for flood insurance but not participating in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition applies one year after the community has been formally notified by FEMA of the designation. Exceptions: not applicable to certain State-administered programs (e.g., some CDBG, Rental Rehabilitation, Emergency Shelter Grant allocations) as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-effective-date prohibitions for certain locations and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as listed in §55.12(c), HUD financial assistance (including mortgage insurance) may not be approved after the effective date with respect to: (1) any action (other than a functionally dependent use) located in a floodway; (2) any critical action located in a coastal high hazard area; or (3) any non‑critical action in a coastal high hazard area unless designed for that location or functionally dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An action is considered designed for a coastal high hazard area if new construction/substantial rehabilitation meets current FEMA V-zone standards (44 CFR 60.3(e)) and applicable HUD Minimum Property Standards, or existing construction met applicable FEMA elevation/construction standards at time of original construction or the earliest FEMA standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Coastal high hazard area
rubrics_metrics.description: Area subject to high velocity waters (e.g., hurricane wave wash or tsunamis) designated on FEMA flood maps as Zone V1-30, VE, or V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIRMs and FHBMs shall be relied on for delineation of coastal high hazard areas and other floodplain designations for this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Critical action
rubrics_metrics.description: Any activity for which even a slight chance of flooding would be too great because it might result in loss of life, injury, or property damage. Includes activities that create/maintain/extend useful life of structures that (i) produce/use/store highly volatile/flammable/explosive/toxic/water‑reactive materials; (ii) provide essential/irreplaceable records or utilities/emergency services (e.g., data centers, generating plants, main utility lines, emergency operations centers, sole-egress roadways); or (iii) are likely to contain occupants not sufficiently mobile to avoid loss of life (e.g., hospitals, nursing homes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housing for independent living for the elderly is not a critical action. Critical actions shall not be approved in floodways or coastal high hazard areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: 500-year floodplain as floodplain of concern for Critical Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The 500-year floodplain is the minimum floodplain of concern for Critical Actions and is the area subject to inundation from a flood having a 0.2 percent chance of occurring in any given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §55.2(b)(1) for appropriate data sources (FEMA maps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Floodway
rubrics_metrics.description: Portion of the floodplain effective in carrying flow where flood hazard is generally greatest and water depths/velocities are highest; consistent with FEMA 'regulatory floodways'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Floodways are identified on FEMA maps and are used as the regulatory 'floodway' for prohibitions and review under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Functionally dependent use
rubrics_metrics.description: Land use that must be conducted in close proximity to water (e.g., dam, marina, port facility, waterfront park, many types of bridges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functionally dependent uses may be allowed in some high-hazard locations only if processed under §55.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: High hazard area
rubrics_metrics.description: A floodway or a coastal high hazard area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: New construction (wetlands context)
rubrics_metrics.description: In connection with activities in wetlands, 'new construction' means draining, dredging, channelizing, filling, diking, impounding, and related project construction activities affecting wetlands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 100-year floodplain
rubrics_metrics.description: Floodplain of concern for this part; area subject to a one percent or greater chance of flooding in any given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §55.2(b)(1) for appropriate data sources (FEMA maps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Substantial improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any repair, reconstruction, or improvement of a structure where cost equals or exceeds 50 percent of the market value of the structure before the improvement/repair is started (or, if restoring after damage, before the damage occurred); or any repair/reconstruction/improvement that results in an increase of more than 20 percent in the number of dwelling units in a residential project or in average peak customers/employees on-site for commercial/industrial projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial improvement does not include projects solely to comply with existing health/sanitary/safety codes necessary to assure safe living conditions, nor alterations of structures listed on the National Register of Historic Places or State Historic Inventories. Structural work not meeting this definition is 'minor improvements.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Wetlands (subject to this part)
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas inundated by surface/ground water frequently enough to support vegetation/aquatic life requiring saturated or seasonally saturated soils (e.g., swamps, marshes, bogs, sloughs, potholes, wet meadows, river overflows, mud flats, natural ponds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only wetlands identified/delineated on maps issued by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service or the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers are subject to coverage under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of oversight responsibilities (Assistant Secretary for CPD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant Secretary for Community Planning and Development (CPD) shall oversee the Department's implementation of the Orders and this part in all HUD programs and the implementation activities of HUD program managers and grant recipients for HUD financial assistance subject to 24 CFR part 58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In performing responsibilities, Assistant Secretary shall make pertinent policy determinations, cooperate with program offices, and provide assistance, training, publications, and procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other departmental responsibilities (Assistant Secretaries, General Counsel, GNMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other HUD Assistant Secretaries, the General Counsel, and the President of GNMA shall ensure compliance with this part in actions under their jurisdiction, ensure technical resources are available, and incorporate required criteria/standards/procedures into departmental regulations, handbooks, and project/site standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional and field office responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional Administrators/Regional Housing Commissioners and Field Office Managers shall ensure full implementation of this part in decisions/approvals they are responsible for and monitor actions approved by HUD or grant recipients to ensure prescribed mitigation is implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Certifying Officer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifying Officers of grant recipients administering activities subject to 24 CFR part 58 shall comply with this part in carrying out HUD-assisted programs and monitor approved actions to ensure any prescribed mitigation is implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in accordance with sections of EO 11988 and EO 11990 requiring recipient certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of compliance with part relative to NEPA and HUD approvals (§55.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where environmental review is required under NEPA and 24 CFR part 50 or 58, compliance with this part must be completed before completing an EA (including a FONSI) or an EIS, in accordance with decision points in 24 CFR 50.17(a)-(h), or before preparation of an EA under 24 CFR 58.40 or an EIS under 24 CFR 58.36.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For actions categorically excluded from NEPA under 24 CFR part 50 or 58, compliance with this part must be completed before the Department's initial (SAMA, conditional, etc.) approval or conditional commitment/approval by a grant recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical exclusions do not remove obligations under this part
rubrics_metrics.description: The categorical exclusion of certain proposed actions from NEPA requirements does not exclude those actions from compliance with this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if NEPA review is not required, the floodplain/wetland decisionmaking process must still be followed where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability categories (§55.12) — categories exempt from some/all decision steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of proposed actions are exempt from Steps 2, 3 and 7 (public notice, alternatives, and final notice) or from the decisionmaking process altogether, including specified HUD dispositions, refinancing/purchase under section 223(f), minor repairs not meeting 'substantial improvement' thresholds, HUD-assisted exempt activities, policy-level actions without site decisions, repossessions/foreclosures to protect HUD's financial interests, minor amendments with no additional adverse impacts, project sites with only incidental floodplain/wetland portions meeting strict conditions, interim emergency assistance limited to necessary protection, actions with FEMA LOMA/LOMR removing property from floodplain (subject to conditions), certain previously approved actions, non-site-based voucher/certificate programs, and other listed exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where exemptions apply, specific conditions in §55.12 (including requirements for covenants, drainage, and limits on modification of floodplain/wetland) must be met to avoid processing under §55.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 1: Determine location
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Determine whether the proposed action is located in a wetland or in a 100-year floodplain (or a 500-year floodplain for a Critical Action). If not located in one of those locations, no further compliance with this part is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 2: Early public notice and involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2: Notify the public at the earliest possible time of a proposal to consider an action in a floodplain or wetland (or the 500-year floodplain for a Critical Action), and involve affected/interested public in the decisionmaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must be bilingual if affected public is largely non-English speaking, published in an appropriate local printed medium, and sent to Federal/State/local agencies, organizations, and interested individuals. Minimum 15-calendar-day public comment period. Notice must state name, proposed location/description, total acres of floodplain/wetland involved, HUD official and phone number, and hours/office where full description may be reviewed. Notices may be combined with other project notices where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 3: Identify and evaluate practicable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 3: Identify and evaluate practicable alternatives to locating the proposed action in a floodplain or wetland (or the 500-year floodplain for a Critical Action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternatives including locations outside the floodplain/wetland (or 500-year for Critical Actions), alternative methods to serve the identical project objective, and the determination not to approve any action. Review of practicable alternatives should include feasible technological alternatives, hazard reduction methods and mitigation costs, and environmental impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 4: Identify direct and indirect impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 4: Identify the potential direct and indirect impacts associated with occupancy or modification of the floodplain or wetland (or 500-year floodplain for a Critical Action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 5: Design/modify to minimize adverse impacts and restore/preserve values
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 5: Where practicable, design or modify the proposed action to minimize potential adverse impacts within the floodplain or wetland (including the 500-year floodplain for a Critical Action) and to restore and preserve its natural and beneficial values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Critical Actions in the 500-year floodplain shall be designed or modified to include: (1) preparation of and participation in an early warning system; (2) an emergency evacuation and relocation plan; (3) identification of evacuation routes out of the 500-year floodplain; and (4) identification marks of past or estimated flood levels on all structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 6: Reevaluate practicability and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 6: Reevaluate the proposed action to determine whether it is still practicable given exposure to flood hazards and its potential adverse impacts or to determine whether alternatives preliminarily rejected at Step 3 are practicable in light of information from Steps 4 and 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 7: Final notice when no practicable alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 7: If the reevaluation finds no practicable alternative to locating the proposal in the floodplain or wetland (or the 500-year floodplain for a Critical Action), publish a final notice that includes reasons why the proposal must be located there, a list of alternatives considered, and all mitigation measures to be taken to minimize adverse impacts and restore/preserve values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice procedures of Step 2 apply; provide minimum 7-calendar-day public comment period prior to approval. Include adherence to bilingual and distribution requirements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaking process — Step 8: Implement and ensure continuing responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 8: Upon completion of Steps 1–7, implement the proposed action. There is a continuing responsibility to ensure the mitigating measures identified in Step 7 are implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved actions must be monitored to ensure mitigation measures are actually carried out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of floodplain hazard to parties and tenants (§55.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: For HUD programs where a financial transaction for a property in a floodplain (500-year for Critical Action) is guaranteed, approved, regulated, or insured, any private party participating in the transaction and any current or prospective tenant must be informed by HUD (or HUD's designee) or a grant recipient of the hazards of the floodplain location before execution of documents completing the transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conveyance restrictions for disposition of real property (§55.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: In disposition (including leasing) of properties acquired by HUD located in a floodplain (500-year for Critical Action) or a wetland, conveyance documents must refer to uses restricted under identified Federal/State/local floodplain or wetland regulations and include land use restrictions limiting property use by grantee/purchaser and successors under State/local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For properties in a 500-year floodplain containing Critical Actions, HUD shall require by covenant or comparable restriction that property owners and successive owners provide written notification to each current and prospective tenant concerning flood hazards and availability of flood insurance on contents; notice must also be posted in the building, legible and easily visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of fund availability (§55.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any HUD document notifying the public of the availability of funds for a program (including eligible organizations, activities, application requirements, and selection criteria) shall indicate that all proposed sites in a floodplain or wetland are subject to compliance with this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant recipients subject to 24 CFR part 58 must also comply with this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of actions (§55.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more actions require compliance with subpart C, affect the same floodplain/wetland, and are currently under review by HUD or a grant recipient, individual or aggregated approvals may be issued. A single compliance review and approval is subject to compliance with the decisionmaking process in §55.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregated approval must still follow the eight-step decision process and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areawide compliance substitution (§55.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: A HUD-approved areawide compliance process may substitute for individual or aggregated compliance where a series of individual actions is proposed/contemplated in a pertinent area; the areawide process must accord with decision process §55.20 and may examine a sector or entire floodplain/wetland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areawide compliance must: consider local land use planning and state programs; develop/publish a strategy identifying development/mitigation measures and actions not approved; be initiated by HUD through a formal agreement with affected local governments; may be joint with other agencies or grant recipients; establish mechanisms ensuring consistency of individual approvals with the areawide strategy, implementation/enforcement, and mitigation as a condition of approval; use open scoping (40 CFR 1501.7); invite Federal/State/local agencies with relevant expertise to scoping; limit eligibility to communities in NFIP Regular Program in good standing; and state an expiration date (<=10 years) with mechanism for HUD reevaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of another agency's prior Executive Orders review (§55.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed action covered under this part is already covered by a prior review under the Executive Orders by another agency, that review may be adopted by HUD or a grant recipient authorized under 24 CFR part 58 provided: (a) no pending litigation relates to the other agency's review; (b) the adopting agency finds the currently proposed action is comparable to the previously reviewed action and there has been no material change in circumstances; and (c) mitigation measures similar to those prescribed in the prior review shall be required as a condition of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements (§55.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible HUD official (or Certifying Officer for a grant recipient) must require documentation for compliance with §55.20, including: (1) identification of practicable alternative sites outside the floodplain/wetland within the appropriate local market/service/jurisdictional area, identification of actual sites under review, and reasons for non-selection; and (2) evidence that measures to minimize adverse impacts identified in Step 4 have been applied to the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also require documentation of compliance with §§55.24–55.26 as appropriate. Documentation (including copies of public notices) must be attached to the EA, EIS, or compliance record and maintained in the project file; for EISs, include documentation in the Record of Decision (or environmental review record for grant recipients).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of part 55 obligations into part 58 and federal authorities listing (§58.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Floodplain management and wetland protection requirements are authorities to be considered under environmental review procedures for HUD-funded community development and rental rehabilitation programs; EO 11988 and EO 11990 as interpreted in 24 CFR part 55 are incorporated into part 58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §55.10 for relationship between the decisionmaking process in 24 CFR part 55 and part 58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site design: elevation requirements for residential structures with basements (§200.926d(c)(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevation of the lowest floor in residential structures with basements located in FEMA-designated areas of special flood hazard shall be at or above the base flood level (100-year flood level) required for new construction or substantial improvement under NFIP regulations (44 CFR 60.3-60.6), except where FEMA variances or exceptions allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variances may be granted by communities under FEMA procedures at 44 CFR 60.6(a) or FEMA may approve exceptions under 44 CFR 60.6(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Site design: elevation requirements for residential structures without basements (§200.926d(c)(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For residential structures without basements in FEMA-designated areas of special flood hazard, the elevation of the lowest floor shall be at or above the FEMA-designated base flood elevation (100-year flood level).

rubrics_metrics.name: Site design: coastal high hazard area prohibitions and elevation (§200.926d(c)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Residential structures located in FEMA-designated 'coastal high hazard areas' — basements or any permanent enclosure of space below the lowest floor are prohibited. Where FEMA has determined base flood level without stillwater elevations, the underside of the lowest floor and its horizontal supports shall be at or above the base flood level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site design: Critical Actions elevation and prohibitions (§200.926d(c)(4)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: For Critical Actions (as defined in 24 CFR 55.2(b)(2)), the lowest floor of a structure (including basement and all mechanical, electrical, and service equipment) shall be at or above the FEMA-designated 500-year flood elevation. Critical Actions located in FEMA-designated floodways and coastal high hazard areas are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site design: street drainage and emergency vehicle passability (§200.926d(c)(4)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Streets must be usable during runoff equivalent to a 10-year return frequency. Where drainage outfall is inadequate to prevent runoff equivalent to a 10-year return frequency from ponding over 6 inches deep, streets must be made passable for commonly used emergency vehicles during runoff equivalent to a 25-year return frequency, except where an alternative access street not subject to such ponding is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site design: crawl space moisture control (§200.926d(c)(4)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Crawl spaces must not pond water or be subject to prolonged dampness.
